preconditions.description: The input consists of exactly two lines: the first line is the integer n, and the second line is the binary string b.
The integer n matches the length of the binary string b, and n is between 1 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(c in '01' for c in lines[1])
preconditions.description: The binary string b contains only the characters '0' and '1'.

postconditions.description: The output is the minimum number of character changes required to eliminate all occurrences of the substring '010' from the input string.

postconditions.expression: min_moves == sum(1 for i in range(len(b) - 2) if b[i:i+3] == '010' and (i == 0 or b[i-1] != '0' or b[i-1:i+1] != '01'))
postconditions.description: The minimum moves count is calculated by greedily identifying non-overlapping '010' patterns and counting them, where a pattern at index i is counted only if it is not part of a previously handled overlapping pattern (specifically, if the previous character was not '0' or the previous two characters were not '01', ensuring we skip the overlapping '10' part of a previous '010' fix).
